transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Mark Delgado (Lumen CTO), Sara Kim (Eng Manager), Victor Huang (Platform Lead), Emily Ross (Procurement)
Notes/Links: benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/lumen-proposal (shared in chat) ; security pack link: /docs/redwood-security.pdf

Summary: Quick scoping to agree success criteria, workload sizing, and an initial POC timeline with milestones (kickoff, access setup, midpoint review, exec readout). Customer wants to validate latency at 99th percentile, unit cost targets, and data residency guarantees. Agreed on 3-week run with dedicated capacity option for baseline tests.

Topics: success criteria; dataset and QPS sizing; benchmark plan; timeline and milestones; security/access requirements; procurement/contract timing.

Transcript:
00:00 Alex Mercer: hey everyone um thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood. quick roll call?
00:07 Mark Delgado: yep mark here, sara, victor and emily also on the call.
00:12 Priya Singh: priya from the se team, i'll be leading the benchmarks and test plan.
00:18 Sara Kim: great, thanks. high level, we want to validate two things - latency at p99 under our expected load and token cost per 1k for the claim summarization pipeline.
00:29 Alex Mercer: perfect, that's helpful. can you remind us of expected qps and document sizes?
00:34 Victor Huang: most requests are batch-ish — the frontline service will send 10–20 concurrent requests, each request averages 1.2k tokens after prompt + context. Peak qps ~12. sustained ~4.
00:45 Priya Singh: okay so peak concurrency 12, avg request 1.2k tokens, noted. are you ok with a dedicated node for the baseline or do you want hosted?
00:53 Mark Delgado: procurement prefers hosted to start but engineering wants the dedicated numbers — if you can run both that would be ideal.
01:02 Alex Mercer: yeah we can do a TWO-phased POC: 1) hosted baseline to validate end-to-end latency and correctness, 2) dedicated capacity run for throughput and cost modeling.
01:14 Sara Kim: success criteria — p99 under 500ms for short form replies, for these long 1.2k token flows we expect p95 < 1.2s and p99 < 2.5s. cost goal is below $0.20 per 1k tokens processed in production mix.
01:30 Priya Singh: that gives us concrete targets. we'll run two benchmark suites: latency-focused and cost/throughput focused. will include KV cache priming test and prefix caching.
01:42 Victor Huang: on the data side we need to keep everything in our region and have KMS keys in our account — is private deployment required for that?
01:50 Alex Mercer: you can do region-located hosted with customer-managed KMS (we support cross-account KMS) for many customers; private VPC deployment works too but needs procurement/contract lead time. we should decide after the kickoff when we see initial latencies.
02:05 Emily Ross: on contracts, procurement timeline is 4 weeks from SOW acceptance. we'd likely need SOC2 + a DPA in place.
02:13 Alex Mercer: we have SOC2 docs and a DPA template; i'll include those in the follow-up pack.
02:20 (sound of keyboard)
02:28 Priya Singh: for benchmarking — i propose the following milestones: kickoff & access setup (week 1), baseline hosted tests (days 3–5), dedicated capacity runs (week 2), midpoint review with results and ask (end of week 3), then exec readout and decision week 5.
02:45 Mark Delgado: that timeline works if we can get staging data quickly. we'll need a clear runbook for the data sanitization step.
02:54 Priya Singh: we'll provide a runbook and a small sanitizer script; you can run locally or we can run in your staging account with least-privilege roles.
03:05 Victor Huang: if you run benchmarks in our account we need a short maintenance window, and we'll provide an IAM role with STS.
03:14 Alex Mercer: fine — for the dedicated run we'll need access to the staging S3 and an exec IAM role. we'll provide a checklist for required permissions.
03:23 Sara Kim: can you confirm which model families you'll test and whether quantized variants are included?
03:29 Priya Singh: we'll test 3 model points: a performant open model (redwood-compat-small), a mid-size quality model (redwood-compat-medium-quant), and a high-quality variant. quantized runs will be in dedicated phase to show cost delta.
03:45 Mark Delgado: curious about fallback behavior — if dedicated capacity fills up, what's the failover?
03:51 Alex Mercer: routing policy can fallback to hosted or to a smaller model family; we'll include that in runbook. also for throttling we can simulate burst traffic.
04:03 Emily Ross: on procurement again — can you share an estimated POC cost range?
04:08 Alex Mercer: i'll send a pricing matrix; rough estimate for a 3-week dedicated baseline is in the ballpark of $8–12k depending on instance choices. hosted baseline is significantly lower.
04:20 Priya Singh: technical note — we'll capture detailed telemetry (per-token latency, batch sizes, kv cache hit rates). please confirm you can expose the request traces or logs we need.
04:31 Victor Huang: yes we can share logs, but logs must be scrubbed and we prefer S3 with KMS-managed encryption.
04:38 Priya Singh: noted, we'll adapt. also we'll provide a benchmark artifact spreadsheet (link shared) with test vectors and expected metrics so everyone can follow.
04:48 (brief pause)
04:55 Alex Mercer: ok let's agree on concrete milestones — kickoff week of 2026-04-06, access/setup completed by 2026-04-08, baseline hosted tests 2026-04-09–2026-04-11, dedicated runs 2026-04-13–2026-04-19, midpoint review 2026-04-27, exec readout week of 2026-05-11.
05:18 Sara Kim: agreed, we'll aim to provide staging access by 2026-04-05 as discussed.
05:24 Emily Ross: procurement will review SOW as soon as you share it; expect a 2–4 week internal review.
05:30 Alex Mercer: i'll follow up with SOW + pricing + SOC2 pack + runbook. Priya will send the benchmark plan and test vectors.
05:36 Priya Singh: action items noted, i'll also include a short runbook for cache priming.
05:41 Mark Delgado: great. one more ask — for the midpoint review can you include a quick TCO slide comparing hosted vs dedicated with expected savings at scale?
05:50 Alex Mercer: yes, we'll include TCO and expected break-even points.
05:55 Alex Mercer: ok thanks everyone — we'll send the follow ups and i'll set the kickoff calendar invite.
05:59 (call ends)

Recap: Agreed POC goals (p99/p95 latency targets, cost per 1k token goal), agreed dataset/access needs, 3-week run with hosted baseline + dedicated phase, midpoint review and exec readout schedule. Redwood to send pricing, SOW, runbook, and benchmark plan; Lumen to provide staging data and IAM/KMS details.

Attachments referenced: redwood_poc_pricing.xlsx (link in chat), lumen_benchmark_vectors.csv, redwood-security-pack.pdf
